examples.knowledge_point: Solving a Polynomial Inequality Containing No Constant Term
examples.worked_solution:
To solve the inequality $f(x) \gt 0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y = f(x)$ lies above the $x$-axis.

First, we factor the polynomial $f(x){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={x}^{3}-9x \\  & =x({x}^{2}-9) \\  & =x(x+3)(x-3)\end{aligned}
$$

The roots of the polynomial $f(x) = x^3 - 9x$ are $x= - 3,$ $x=0,$ and $x = 3,$ which are all simple roots.

So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14007649/assets/91e0e81b98e7f89796c277854bec6ce0240c797fc0c3d1eda3f33ce4bc9c85a6.png)

Since we are interested in solving $f(x) \gt 0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is above the $x$-axis.

Based on the graph, the solution is 

$$
x \in (-3,0) \cup (3,\infty).
$$

feedback.problem: Given the polynomial $P(x)=x(x+3)^{4}(x-1),$ find the solution of $P(x)>0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To solve the inequality $P(x)>0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y=P(x)$ lies above the $x$-axis.

The roots of the polynomial $P(x)=x(x+3)^{4}(x-1)$ are $x=-3,x=0$ and $x=1,$ where

- $x=-3$ has multiplicity $4,$ and

- $x=0$ and $x=1$ are simple roots.

Also, $P(x)$ is a polynomial of degree $6$ with a positive leading coefficient. So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14007649/assets/6938cb283f25ccc325d7f50fcd793f1b9928025218bb6e9ca08f2d3941d16690.png)

Since we are interested in solving $P(x)>0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is above the $x$-axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\in (-\infty ,-3)\cup (-3,0)\cup (1,\infty ).$
